program.program_name: Auto Body Repair and Refinishing Technician Foundation

offerings.status: Refer to official BCIT program page

courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course introduces students to WorkSafeBC's Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) regulations and the Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS). Students will learn how the regulations apply to their workplace environment. This course also covers the proper use of personal protection equipment, general shop safety procedures, and fire safety procedures. Prerequisite(s): Entry to the program.

​This course introduces students to the safe use, handling, and care of various tools and equipment used in the collision repair and refinishing industry. The safe and acceptable work habits learned in theory will be applied in the shop environment. Prerequisite(s): ABRR 1500

​This course introduces students to understand the documentation and procedures used to ensure the repair of vehicles is carried out correctly and efficiently. The student will be introduced to the trade terminology and vehicle information required to conduct repairs as per customer or insurance company requirements. Students will also learn how to perform visual inspections on coatings and repairs performed to the vehicle. Prerequisite(s): ABRR 1500

​This course introduces students how to effectively communicate in the work environment with the employer and fellow employees. The student will also understand the roles and responsibilities of workers in the Auto Body trade and be able describe business and workplace relations. The student will also prepare a resume for employability readiness. Prerequisite(s): ABRR 1500

​Upon completion of this course, students will be able to safely use oxyacetylene welding and cutting equipment for cutting and heating. Students will also be able to demonstrate the use of GMAW welding equipment and Plasma arc cutting equipment. Prerequisite(s): ABRR 1500

​This course introduces students to procedures required to effectively identify and remove or replace various components to the vehicles interior and exterior during the repair and refinishing process. Furthermore, the student will learn techniques used to remove and re-apply decals and stripes to the exterior of the vehicle body. Prerequisite(s): ABRR 1500

​This work practicum gives students the opportunity to apply their knowledge at a collision repair facility. The related work experience reinforces material presented in the program and enhances their skills and abilities through interaction with experienced tradespeople. Prerequisite(s): ABRR 1500

​This course introduces the student to follow the correct steps to perform a repair to a damaged exterior body panel. Students will learn how to mix and apply body fillers and primer undercoats to selected panels and prepare panels for the application of undercoats using spraying equipment in a spray booth. Prerequisite(s): ABRR 1500

courses.course_name: Remove, Repair and Install Metal Panels and Components
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course introduces students to various categories of vehicle construction and the different methods required to repair each type of vehicle. The course emphasizes an understanding of the materials used in construction, and how to repair, replace and re- align such components. Prerequisite(s): ABRR 1500

​This second two-week work practicum gives students the opportunity to apply their knowledge at a collision repair facility. The related work experience reinforces material presented in the program and enhances their skills and abilities through interaction with experienced tradespeople. Prerequisite(s): ABRR 1500

courses.course_name: Remove, Repair and Install Plastic and Composite Panels and Components
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course introduces students to various categories of plastics and composite materials found on vehicles with the emphasis to enable the student to understand and perform repairs, replacement and re-alignment of each type of material. Students will perform a variety of repairs to plastics panels using current repair standards and equipment. Prerequisite(s): ABRR 1500

​This course introduces students to methods used to prepare vehicle surfaces prior to the application of paint coatings. The learner will have the opportunity to become familiar with the steps involved to clean, prepare and sand the various substrates found on vehicles such as steel, aluminum and composites and plastics. Additionally, the learner will also demonstrate masking procedures prior to the application of paint coatings. Prerequisite(s): ABRR 1500

​This course introduces students to the cleaning and preparation of panels and vehicle parts prior to applying various types of primers and topcoats on vehicles. Students will learn about different topcoat systems and how to apply them to a prepared substrate. Prerequisite(s): ABRR 1500

​This third, two-week work practicum gives students the opportunity to apply their knowledge at a collision repair facility. The related work experience reinforces material presented in the program and enhances their skills and abilities through interaction with experienced tradespeople. Prerequisite(s): ABRR 1500

admission.raw: Note: This trade program is in high demand. Visit Trades Training BC to estimate a future start date. Scheduled intakes September and January each year. *Scheduled intakes are subject to change. Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first qualified basis as long as space remains. When available intakes are full, qualified applicants are wait-listed. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements prior to applying to this program. If you are uncertain or don’t meet the requirements we strongly recommend you complete any applicable Trades Entry Assessments before applying. English language proficiency: one of the following: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent or BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment Math: one of the following: Foundations of Math and Pre-Calculus 10 (50%) or Workplace Math 10 (50%) or Other acceptable BC and Yukon courses or BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Recommended for success A driver’s licence is strongly recommended in order to move vehicles in and out of the shops. Potential applicants with medical or physical disabilities should contact Accessibility Services to arrange an interview with the institute's rehabilitation specialist at 604-451-6963 (telephone interview is acceptable for out of town applicants). Trades Discovery The Trades Discovery General and Trades Discovery for Women are full-time programs designed to prepare participants to successfully enter and complete a Trades Training program. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks.
